paper_metadata.title: Microstructure and Property-Based Statistically Equivalent Representative Volume Elements for Polycrystalline Ni-Based Superalloys Containing Annealing Twins

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: This paper has three major objectives related to the development of computational micromechanics models of Ni-based superalloys, containing a large number of annealing twins.

evidence.section: IV. VALIDATION OF THE VIRTUAL MICROSTRUCTURE GENERATION ALGORITHM USING EBSD DATA
evidence.quote: The model and algorithms are validated using the EBSD data of the Ni-based superalloy specimen, discussed in Section II–A.

evidence.section: VII. CONCLUSIONS
evidence.quote: This paper develops a methodology for generating 3D statistically equivalent virtual polycrystalline microstructures (3D-SEVPMs) of polycrystalline Ni-based superalloys containing annealing twins, which are critical determinants of failure mechanisms such as fatigue cracks.

evidence.section: II. MICROSTRUCTURAL IMAGE EXTRACTION AND MECHANICAL TESTING
evidence.quote: A 10 × 5 × 1 μm sample was sectioned from a forging of the superalloy René-88 DT using wire electrical discharge machining (EDM).

evidence.section: VI. PROPERTY-BASED SERVE (P-SERVE) AND ITS ESTIMATION
evidence.quote: the parameters of the AE-CP constitutive model are directly calibrated from experimental data on polycrystalline superalloy Rene88-DT.

evidence.section: VII. CONCLUSIONS
evidence.quote: This paper develops a methodology for generating 3D statistically equivalent virtual polycrystalline microstructures (3D-SEVPMs) of polycrystalline Ni-based superalloys containing annealing twins, which are critical determinants of failure mechanisms such as fatigue cracks.

evidence.section: VII. CONCLUSIONS
evidence.quote: The parent grain size is found to be strongly correlated to the number of twins. The number of twins per parent increases with the parent grain size, and approximately 50 pct of the parent grains are untwinned.

evidence.section: VII. CONCLUSIONS
evidence.quote: Finally, while the M-SERVE and P-SERVE are relatively small compared to the scale of the grain structure for these properties, other properties such as fatigue may require larger volumes of the material to be analyzed.
